operation.body:
## Goal
Implement the adopted D-020 fixed-selector native sysctl inventory reader behind the existing typed contract, with safe C storage, Swift normalization, fake-native validation and Intel build/CI integration. Deliver one coherent PR without invoking live telemetry.

## Acceptance criteria
- Implement only the seven approved selectors with sysctlbyname(fixedName, boundedInitializedBuffer, &length, NULL, 0). No arbitrary names, setters, shell, privilege, SMC, retries, allocation growth or live invocation. Reject invalid field/capacity before a syscall.
- Audit SDK declarations and exact call reachability. Preserve native status/length checks, fixed errno classification, no failed partial data, integer widths and exact UInt64 values. Retain fixed provenance/reasons and existing string/count validation.
- Add a Swift reader conforming to PublicInventoryReader and a minimal C boundary. Keep native access separate from the synthetic CLI; no static initialization reads. Explain future worker/report JSON integration without enabling it.
- Fake-native tests exercise the real C implementation's selector/arguments/buffers, errno failures, lengths and widths; Swift fixtures verify bridge integration, malformed data, fixed gaps and JSON. Tests must never call real sysctl. Integrate both SwiftPM and direct x86_64 macOS 12 builds into existing Intel CI, preserving all checks.
- Update development and adopted design/architecture status honestly. Complete independent integrated review, signed commits, exact-head green CI and human review/merge handoff. No target compatibility or deadline guarantee.

## Constraints
Parent Project #1; current local self-correcting-review auto-merge invocation. Scope follows owner priority update 2026-11-15 and adopted D-019/D-020. Native/input-validation code is High risk and requires human review and human merge; auto-merge is ineligible. Existing design adoption permits implementation without repeated approval. Preserve private workflow, historical evidence and unrelated .gitlab/.
Risks: accidental setter arguments, unchecked lengths/partial storage, ABI width/byte order, errno leakage, fixture tests accidentally invoking hardware, compilation confused with Monterey validation. Decision queue: no blocking choice; worker/deadline/IPC, other native sources, secure persistence and runtime remain later adopted-design increments. Rollback: reviewed forward revert PR; no installed service or report storage.

## Out of scope
Live telemetry invocation or hardware/capture tests (including during CI), workloads, privilege, SMC, fan writes/control, native CPU-tick/thermal/battery/OS-version readers, workers/IPC/session implementation, persistence, live CLI wiring, new dependencies/toolchain installation, GUI/recovery, background automation and a second goal.

## Relevant context
Project #1 current scope; D-019/D-020; docs/public-telemetry-adapter-review.md; docs/discovery-specification.md; docs/development.md; Sources/DiscoveryCore/PublicInventory.swift; .ai/project/ and .ai/docs/project-requirements.md. Goals 2,7,9,11,13,15,17,19,21,23 terminal via merged PRs 3,8,10,12,14,16,18,20,22,24. Authoritative main eb5849a0118d13a281a333de06a949bff33cfe2f has successful CI 43745100249; no deferred owner-validation checks.
